service.name: Wedding and corporate event DJ
service.serviceType: Open-format DJ for weddings, corporate events, late-night receptions and private parties
service.description: Open-format DJ for wedding receptions, corporate events and private parties across Denver and the Colorado mountain corridor, on its own or carrying the late night after a band through the same sound system on one contract.

faqs.q: Can the DJ follow the band on the same contract?
faqs.a: Yes. Once we're in the building the evening is already committed, so adding the DJ to a band booking costs far less than hiring one separately would, through the same sound system and on the same contract. The handoff is planned with your run of show.

faqs.q: Do you DJ weddings as well as corporate events?
faqs.a: Yes. The wedding booking usually starts at the end of dinner, with live musicians in front of it for the ceremony and the cocktail hour, and the DJ carrying the floor from the first dance to the last song. It's the same open-format set, the same sound system and the same contract as the corporate night.

faqs.q: What does the DJ booking include?
faqs.a: Decks, booth and a PA that's the right size for the venue, an announcement microphone, load-in and strike, a certificate of insurance and a W-9.

faqs.q: How late can the DJ play?
faqs.a: As late as the venue allows. Added time comes in half-hour blocks, and you can decide it on the night. Venue curfews and decibel caps are built into the plan.

faqs.q: What is the DJ plus live instrument option?
faqs.a: A live bass or saxophone played on the floor over the set. It's the difference between a playlist and a crowd watching something happen, and it holds a dance floor late. It's an option, quoted when you ask for it.

faqs.q: Do you take requests on the night?
faqs.a: From you, always, and from guests where they fit. A do-not-play list is the part worth spending time on before the event. A request that would empty the floor gets a straight answer and an alternative.
